title: A Contact for the Protocol
premise: Yara Thackeray, a hostage negotiator haunted by a botched exchange that cost a life five years ago, receives a voiceprint-verified call from a whistleblower embedded in a covert intelligence-sharing program called the Protocol. The voiceprint belongs to the negotiator she failed to save — or someone using his voice — and it unlocks a server in Nairobi exposing three governments' complicity in staged terror events. Hunted by an assassin contracted to bury the leak and disavowed by her own agency, Yara must shepherd the whistleblower and the evidence across borders while deciding whether loyalty to the institution that trained her matters more than the truth. In the end, Yara trades herself as a hostage to force a public hearing, exposing the Protocol at the cost of her career — and discovers the voice was real: the man she failed survived, and his survival was the first lie the Protocol ever told her.
about_author: Lena Okonkwo is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to people talk their way out of impossible corners before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about institutions, voices on the phone, and the price of being believed.

chapters.title: The Voice on Line Two
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. During a routine bank-siege negotiation in Manchester, an unknown caller hijacks her secure line with a voiceprint match to Daniel Okafor — the hostage who died on her watch five years ago. He gives her a server address and one sentence: 'You already have clearance.' Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Cold Board
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She reports the anomaly internally and is quietly suspended pending a 'voice-authenticity review' — standard procedure, her supervisor says, but the review team arrives within hours, too fast for procedure. Emotional beat: the slow realization that the rules are being rewritten around her in real time.

chapters.title: Nairobi, 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Amara's POV — introduced here, a forensic linguist in Nairobi who authenticated the voiceprint and is now being questioned by men without badges. She uploads a partial archive to a dead-drop server and goes dark. Emotional beat: professional calm cracking into fear as she realizes what the files describe.

chapters.title: What the Server Says
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, accessing the drop from a hotel business center. Staged incidents, laundered informants, three governments trading deniability like currency — and her own name in a personnel annex marked 'expendable, retained.' Emotional beat: cold clarity; belonging revealed as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Dead
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV, first appearance. Alive under a new identity, he explains via burner phone why he let the world believe he died: his 'death' was the Protocol's pilot test of narrative control. He needs Yara because her failure is the story's anchor. Emotional beat: fury and relief tangled together.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Voss's POV — the assassin, methodical and oddly principled, briefed to retrieve the archive and leave no witnesses. He maps Yara's routines with unsettling patience. Emotional beat: dread built from competence; we see exactly how good the threat is.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She meets Amara in person in Lisbon after Amara flees Nairobi; they argue about going public versus going official. Yara still believes in channels. Emotional beat: two kinds of faith in systems colliding over bad hotel coffee.

chapters.title: Lisbon Lockdown
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The safehouse meeting is compromised — not by Voss, but by a second team, revealing the Protocol doesn't fully trust its own contractor. Voss spares them, technically completing his contract by letting another fail. Emotional beat: moral static inside a professional killer.

chapters.title: Expendable, Retained
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Her mentor, Deputy Director Hale, offers reinstatement if she hands over the archive and recants. He genuinely believes he's saving her. Emotional beat: loyalty offered as a trap with soft lining; Yara declines and burns her last bridge.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Story
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The trio pieces together how each government's version of events interlocks, realizing no single leak will suffice — the story must land simultaneously in all three jurisdictions. Emotional beat: the scale of the problem becoming clear, and grim laughter as a coping mechanism.

chapters.title: The Ferry to Tangier
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Crossing to Morocco with the archive split across three drives and three people, Yara runs a negotiation exercise on a hostile customs officer purely from habit — and it works. Emotional beat: her disgraced skill set becoming their lifeline.

chapters.title: Voss Closes Distance
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He corners Daniel alone in a medina courtyard and, instead of killing him, asks one question: what does the archive say about him? Daniel shows him. Voss walks away off-contract. Emotional beat: the hunter discovering he is also a subject of the file.

chapters.title: Hostage of One
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To buy time when the second team traps them, Yara negotiates her own detention — talking armed men into holding her instead of shooting, stalling until Amara moves the drives. Emotional beat: her defining skill turned inward; power and humiliation in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Hearing That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. A sympathetic journalist arranges contact with a parliamentary oversight staffer, but the meeting is recorded by Protocol assets and 'leaked' to discredit them preemptively. Emotional beat: watching truth get pre-poisoned; despair at how easily narratives are weaponized.

chapters.title: Split Routes
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. The trio splits: Daniel takes the decoy drive toward Madrid, knowing he'll be taken. His capture is deliberate — bait, bought with his freedom. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy; the man who faked death now spending his real one.

chapters.title: Interrogation, Politely
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV, in custody. A Protocol handler offers him his old name back if he authenticates a doctored version of the archive. He stalls using negotiation techniques Yara taught him years ago. Emotional beat: the student's tools keeping the teacher's failure alive.

chapters.title: Everything Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With Voss now feeding them Protocol movement data, Yara choreographs the triple release: Amara to Nairobi press, the journalist in London, Voss himself delivering the original drives to a Hague prosecutor. Emotional beat: terrified precision; the plan only works if everyone holds.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Yara's POV. The Protocol attempts one final trade: Daniel's release for the Hague drives. Yara negotiates the exchange live, on-record, ensuring every word is witnessed — turning a backroom deal into public testimony. Emotional beat: her greatest negotiation, performed as an act of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: What Breaks
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The Protocol orders Voss to kill everyone at the exchange anyway. He refuses on-record, citing his own file as evidence, and stands down his replacement team by identifying them aloud. Emotional beat: the instrument of erasure choosing witness over silence.

chapters.title: Aftermath, On the Record
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. The hearings begin; Hale resigns rather than testify; two governments issue carefully hollow statements. Amara watches her testimony get absorbed into institutional machinery — real but incomplete. Emotional beat: victory with an asterisk; justice arriving partially, late, and real.

chapters.title: Reinstated, Declined
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Offered her old job back with commendation, Yara instead accepts a role training negotiators — teaching the rules while telling students which ones will be rewritten. She visits Daniel, who is rebuilding a life under yet another name, this time chosen by him. Emotional beat: belonging redefined on her own terms.

chapters.title: A Contact for the Protocol
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV. Months later, an encrypted line rings with a new voiceprint — someone else trapped inside a system that lies. Yara answers, and this time she knows exactly what answering costs. Emotional beat: quiet resolve; the loop continues, but now she chooses it, carrying truth past every wall that gets rebuilt.
